verdict.classification: pre-window legacy failures and whole-suite timing/process instability
verdict.summary: No failure has a credible causal link to a daily candidate. Twenty-two exact names already failed in committed September 6 evidence, and an independently running exact-98cc89c3 suite repeated 27 of the requested 32 before this ledger was finalized. The remaining ten execute test and primary callsite blobs introduced in June-August and unchanged across the daily window; where their exact failure onset was not captured before the window, they are conservatively labeled legacy/unchanged rather than directly reproduced pre-window failures. The only two changed primary paths are a behavior-preserving environment-key helper extraction and the compiled-test import rewriter; neither matches the symptoms, and the same dominant failure families predate both patches.

isolatedRerun.interpretation: The same source switches between pass and fail under different suite schedules, while four process/race cases remain reproducible even in the historical isolated set.

sameDayEarlierSavedRun.interpretation: Twenty-five requested failures recur, while both runs also contain different failures in the same CLI/OpenCode/HSR timing families. This is evidence of schedule-sensitive whole-suite behavior, not evidence of a candidate regression.

independentExactFrozenMainRun.qualifier: This independently establishes exact frozen-main recurrence for 27 cases. It does not by itself establish pre-window age; that conclusion comes from the September 6 evidence and path history above. This review did not launch the run.

supplementalNotUsedForPreWindowAttributi.qualifier: This proves equality across the later repaired controls only. It is supplemental and was not used to claim that failures predate the daily window.

candidateIntersection.method: Union each exact coverage candidate's full -m diff paths and intersect with 24 failing tests plus 40 primary harness/callsite paths.

families.observedPattern: missing compiled v2 CLI artifact, CLI child timeout/exit, or compiled/source entry disagreement under the concurrent legacy suite
families.preWindowAssessment: Eight exact names in this family already fail in the September 6 default run; most pass in the historical isolated rerun. The x and frame cases passed historically but use identical test/command blobs and fail as sibling process timeouts in the saved runs.

families.observedPattern: 30-second command timeout, a five-second fail-fast timing oracle missed by 1.47 seconds, and an eight-second daemon state-file startup timeout
families.preWindowAssessment: Fork and daemon failures are exact September 6 matches. The node timeout recurs in both saved current runs, but has no exact pre-window failure record; its test dates to June and its command path is unchanged.

families.observedPattern: the deliberately tiny 20 ms final credential-sync budget expires under suite load
families.preWindowAssessment: Both exact failures occur in the September 6 default run and pass in its isolated rerun.

families.observedPattern: two file-worker failures without subtest diagnostics and one 60-second event-compaction timeout
families.preWindowAssessment: All three exact file/name outcomes occur in the September 6 default run.

families.observedPattern: point-in-time high-water, next-tool event, and backpressure scheduling assertions
families.preWindowAssessment: All three exact failures occur in the September 6 default run; all can pass in historical isolated execution, while the gateway reconnect assertion also failed in the isolated run and on a fifth pristine-baseline repetition.

families.observedPattern: the fake OpenCode server does not publish its startup URL within 1500-2000 ms
families.preWindowAssessment: These exact names were not recorded failing before the window. The complete test and adapter blobs have been unchanged since August; the earlier saved current run fails six different tests in this same file at roughly the same 3.2-3.6 second startup boundary, which supports file-level process contention rather than a candidate code change.

families.observedPattern: a real child remoteHost serve process does not expose its Unix socket within the test's eight-second wait
families.preWindowAssessment: The exact backfill name lacks a pre-window failure record; the subscribe/replay name recurs in both saved current runs. All test and primary source blobs date to July-August and are unchanged across the window.

families.observedPattern: delayed process-group ownership sampling and descendant-stop deadlines
families.preWindowAssessment: Both exact failures occur in the September 6 default run, the isolated rerun, and the pristine 8506467f residual control.

families.observedPattern: the guard file was already removed when assert.rejects expected ENOENT from a later read
families.preWindowAssessment: No exact pre-window failure record. The test and implementation are the same d631c4d6 blobs from August 7 and no daily candidate touches them.

families.observedPattern: test-finally recursive removal races a still-active background writer and reports ENOTEMPTY
families.preWindowAssessment: The pool case is an exact September 6 and pristine-baseline residual failure. The transcript ownership case recurs in both saved current runs but has no exact pre-window failure record; its test and callsite blobs are unchanged since July-August.

commands.command: git log ae93050e --reverse -S '<test title>' -- <test path>; git log -1 ae93050e -- <source paths>
commands.purpose: date the ten non-exact cases and their primary source paths before the window

limitations: The requested log does not embed its source SHA. The worktree was at 0472a91c99d7a75c19429b6bffc9988e57c2a272 when inspected; its only changes from frozen main are v2 review fixes, and none of the 24 failing tests or 40 primary paths differs from frozen main beyond the two already classified paths.

Failures 2, 7, 10, 19, 20, 21, 23, 24, 29, and 32 have no saved exact same-name failure before the window. Their legacy attribution is based on identical pre-window test/callsite blobs, zero causal candidate diffs, recurring sibling-family failures, and current-run schedule variation; it is not represented as an exact pre-window runtime reproduction.
The three file-level worker failures expose no subtest stack, so this review can attribute their age but cannot isolate their internal failing assertion from the saved log alone.

HBworker's independently launched exact-98cc89c3 run completed while this ledger was being finalized. Its 48 failures and 27/32 overlap are recorded as frozen-main recurrence only, not as proof of pre-window age.
No benchmark, focused test, or full suite was rerun by this review, per the read-only/no-rerun constraint.
